rows: What is Hortonian vs. Dunne overland flow?
Hortonian: rain > infiltration rate; Dunne: saturation excess (soil full)
Higher CN → more runoff; CN=100 → all rain runs off; CN=30 → little runoff
Lower CN (interception, high infiltration) → less runoff vs. cropland or urban
Linear impulse response of a catchment to 1 mm of direct runoff — it's a transfer function
Time of concentration — longest travel time from catchment edge to outlet
Groundwater discharge sustaining river between storms; slow recession curve
Intensity-Duration-Frequency: rainfall intensity vs. storm duration for various return periods
Snow Water Equivalent: water content of snowpack (depth × density)
Relief, soil, and drainage pattern determine runoff response
Rainfall regime and extremes are climate-system outputs
Source-water quality and flow shape treatment design
Infiltration and runoff depend on soil structure and saturation
Stormwater systems are engineered responses to hydrographs
